newsitem.title: USA: Wachovia may seek Fed nod for securities.
newsitem.headline: Wachovia may seek Fed nod for securities.

text.p: Wachovia Corp is proceeding with plans to apply to the Federal Reserve for a Section 20 securities affiliate which could be up and running sometime in the first half of 1998.

"We're doing all the internal preparatory work before we start down that path to make sure everybody knows what it entails," Donald Carson, president of Wachovia Capital Markets Inc, said in an interview Tuesday.
Carson said an application will probably be filed in the next 60 days and the unit could begin operations in the first half of next year.

He said Wachovia, a $48.51 billion-asset bank holding company based in Winston-Salem, N.C., will apply for Tier 1 powers, which permit municipal revenue bonds, asset-backed consumer receivables and other activities, as well as Tier 2-A powers for debt securities.
"We would not apply for, or need, the infrastructure for 2-B" which covers equities, Carson said.

Carson said dealing in municipal revenue bonds was "the one area where we know we can make money immediately" if Wachovia had Section 20 powers. "We're in municipal general obligation bonds, (and) we're quite successful in that business. We're missing two-thirds of the market" by not being in municipal revenue bonds.

He added that the principal business of Wachovia Capital Markets is still going to be bank-eligible activities which do not need a Section 20 affiliate. He said Section 20 powers would be "building a utility for the future."

Under Section 20 of the federal Glass-Steagall law, which separates commercial banks and investment banks into distinct businesses, a bank holding company can have an affiliate for securities dealing. However underwriting activty is limited to 25 percent of the gross revenue of the securities unit. The limitation was raised earlier this year from 10 percent.
